compound adjective and noun

made of two or more parts

also compound word, compound interest, composite, chemical compound

classical

Quint. 1.5.3: verba composita, opposed to simplicia (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. compound word: vocābulum compositum
Traupman 224–225
Traupman 294

compositus, composita, compositum

adjective (perfect participle of compōnō), declension

compound (of a word); put together

The grammarians’ word for a compound, against simplex; in general, put together, arranged. A substance made of several is a mixtūra (see combination).

Other words

  • anatocismus, anatocismī m. — compound interest

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.21.11 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 164; Traupman 333

    Greek ἀνατοκισμός, interest on interest; Cicero uses it twice, of a usurious loan.

Examples

  • Prōnōmen est aut simplex aut compositum.

    A pronoun is either simple or compound.Traupman 224

  • centēsimae cum anatocismō anniversāriō

    one per cent a month, with interest compounded yearlyCic. Att. 5.21.11 (Lewis & Short)

See also combination, interest.
